messages:
jordan: Quick check — we need to decide how the matcher resolves when a host-regex route and a header-based override both look applicable. I sketched a small proposal below.

maya: TL;DR of the problem? :thinking_face:

jordan: Example: route A: host = /.*\\.example.com/ -> service alpha
route B: host = *.example.com, header 'x-target-service: beta' -> service beta (override)
If both match, which route should win? Today order is nondeterministic in some edge cases.

josh: If header explicitly claims a service we generally intended that to override, but that breaks the host-specificity guarantees.

priya: This shows up in console rollouts where canary injects header to divert traffic. We need deterministic rules + observable reason in the UI (why a request routed to X).

alex: Proposal: compute a specificity score composed of: host specificity score + path specificity + explicit header-override bonus. Higher score wins. Host exact > host wildcard > host-regex. Path length adds small weight. Header override adds a fixed bonus only if header value maps to a declared service target for that route.

maya: Can you show pseudocode? Helps for edgecases (regex vs wildcard)

jordan: Sure — rough:

```
score(route, request) = host_score(route.host, request.host)
                        + path_score(route.path, request.path)
                        + (route.header_override && request.headers[route.header_key]==route.header_value ? HEADER_BONUS : 0)

host_score: exact_match=100, wildcard=70, regex=50
path_score: matched_length
HEADER_BONUS = 30
```

josh: With those numbers, an exact host without header beats a wildcard+header in many cases, which sounds right. But regex can be tricky — a wide regex might still truth-match many hosts.

priya: Important: console should surface the components so we can debug (e.g., show host_score/path_score/header_bonus and which rule won). Also, telemetry: sample full traces for first 1% of requests for new rollout rules.

alex: Edgecases: multiple routes could tie. Tie-breaker order: 1) higher host_score 2) longer path 3) lower creation_ts (older wins) 4) config-id deterministic hash. Avoid randomness.

maya: What about query params and header wildcards? We occasionally have routes that match on header prefix or regex.

jordan: Header override only grants bonus if the override maps exactly to the service name in the route config. For header regex/prefix matches we treat that as lower bonus (e.g., HEADER_BONUS/2). Query params are ignored in core scoring unless route explicitly declares query-match — those add small path_score.

josh: Can we keep backward compatibility? Some customers depend on current tie behavior.

jordan: Plan: default to new scoring but gate via feature-flag workspace-wide for 2 weeks, flip globally after rollout. Also publish migration guide and examples.

priya: Telemetry plan: when feature-flag enabled, add per-request match_reason metadata (host_score/path_score/header_bonus, matched_route_id). Store sampled traces and expose in console route inspector.

infra-bot: test-run: matcher-unit-tests: 26/26 passed, integration-match-sim: 412/412 passed, rollout-sim: 120/120 passed.

alex: Can we add a small invariant test: if route A host is strict superset of route B host and both have no overrides, A should never win if B is strictly more specific.

jordan: Yep. I'll draft RFC with pseudocode, test matrix, and console UI mockup. I'll add specific numeric weights and tie-break order. 

maya: One more ask — add an opt-in debug header `x-route-debug=1` that returns match_reason in response for dev testing.

josh: +1 for `x-route-debug` but rate-limit it. Also log to trace only when header present.

priya: Great — put RFC up this week and ping product for UX signoff. :thumbsup:

jordan: Will do. Thanks all.
